about: Hand-gathered exact dates for scripts/build-almanac.py, each with its source. Releases: the first release of a Crate album, kept only when the day is documented (Wikidata publication date with day precision, or two agreeing sources such as the label, the Wikipedia infobox and MusicBrainz); month-only and conflicting dates are left out, as are the release dates of later compilations and reissues. Milestones: jazz.json milestones (by title) with a documented day; one with a Crate album becomes a 'recorded' event on that album with its hand-written line, one without an album is 'held' until the app has a milestone kind.

milestones.source: Wikipedia, Livery Stable Blues: recorded by the Original Dixieland Jass Band on February 26, 1917
Wikipedia, Crazy Blues: Mamie Smith and Her Jazz Hounds recorded it on August 10, 1920

milestones.line: On this day in 1925, Louis Armstrong cut his first Hot Five sides in Chicago, the records that made the improvising soloist jazz's main event.
milestones.source: Wikipedia, Louis Armstrong and His Hot Five: the first sides were recorded on November 12, 1925, at OKeh's Chicago studio
Wikipedia, Cotton Club: Ellington's orchestra was the house band from December 4, 1927

milestones.line: On this day in 1928, Louis Armstrong and His Hot Five recorded West End Blues, opening cadenza and all.
milestones.source: Wikipedia, West End Blues: made by Louis Armstrong and His Hot Five on June 28, 1928
Wikipedia, Palomar Ballroom: Benny Goodman began his first Palomar engagement on August 21, 1935

milestones.line: On this day in 1939, Coleman Hawkins recorded Body and Soul, a ballad improvisation so bold it became an unlikely hit.
milestones.source: Wikipedia, Body and Soul (1930 song): recorded by Coleman Hawkins and His Orchestra on October 11, 1939

milestones.line: On this day in 1945, Charlie Parker's first Savoy session as a leader gave the world Ko-Ko and Now's the Time.
milestones.source: Wikipedia, Ko-Ko: recorded November 26, 1945, at WOR Studios, New York

milestones.line: On this day in 1958, João Gilberto recorded Chega de Saudade at Odeon in Rio, bossa nova's first record.
milestones.source: Estado de Minas/UAI, 'Primeira gravação da Bossa Nova completa 60 anos' (July 10, 2018); Milenio, 'La bossa nova cumple 60 años'

milestones.line: On this day in 1965, Getz/Gilberto won the Grammy for Album of the Year.
milestones.source: Wikipedia, 7th Annual Grammy Awards: held April 13, 1965; Album of the Year, Getz/Gilberto
Wikipedia, The Köln Concert: recorded at the Opera House in Cologne on 24 January 1975
Wikipedia, 26th Annual Grammy Awards: held February 28, 1984; Marsalis won jazz and classical soloist awards
Wikipedia, Jazz (miniseries): first aired on PBS on January 8, 2001
Wikipedia, 50th Annual Grammy Awards: held February 10, 2008; Album of the Year, River: The Joni Letters
Wikipedia, 53rd Annual Grammy Awards: held February 13, 2011; Best New Artist, Esperanza Spalding

milestones.line: On this day in 2013, the Robert Glasper Experiment's Black Radio won the Grammy for Best R&B Album.
milestones.source: Wikipedia, 55th Annual Grammy Awards: held February 10, 2013; Best R&B Album, Black Radio
